title: Finite VC dimension versus agnostic computable PAC learning
formal: Does there exist a nonempty decidably representable class \(\mathcal H\) of total computable functions \(\mathbb N\to\{0,1\}\) with finite VC dimension that is not agnostically computably PAC learnable, even by an improper learner? Explicitly, is there such a class for which no total computable learner \(A\) has the following guarantee: for every \(\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)\), some integer \(N\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge N\) and every distribution \(D\) on \(\mathbb N\times\{0,1\}\), \[\Pr_{S\sim D^{n}}\left[L_D(A(S))\le\inf_{h\in\mathcal H}L_D(h)+\varepsilon\right]\ge1-\delta?\] The learner may return any total computable binary predictor, including predictors outside \(\mathcal H\).
why: The result separates statistical learnability from computable learning even when every target has an effective description and arbitrary computable output hypotheses are allowed. It shows that finite VC dimension alone does not guarantee an implementable agnostic learner, independently of polynomial-time hardness.
status_note: Resolved affirmatively by Sterkenburg, COLT 2022, Theorem 10: a decidably representable class of VC dimension one is not improperly agnostically CPAC learnable. Checked the definitions, theorem and later Hasrati–Ben-David discussion on 2026-09-14. This is a mathematical published resolution, not a claim of an existing Lean proof.

progress.text: Agarwal and coauthors formulate the improper agnostic question and propose a decidably representable candidate of VC dimension one.
Sterkenburg proves Theorem 10, resolving the existence question affirmatively and disproving universal improper CPAC learnability for decidably representable finite-VC classes.
Hasrati and Ben-David discuss this resolved counterexample and prove that it has infinite Littlestone dimension; their separate online-learning questions do not reopen the agnostic PAC question.

importance.reason: A foundational separation between finite statistical complexity and the existence of any computable agnostic learner, surviving improper predictions and decidable target representations; retained as a resolved historical result.

sentences: The question asks whether finite VC dimension and decidable target representations suffice for computable agnostic learning.
Both the learner and every output predictor must halt, but their running times are unrestricted.
Output hypotheses may lie outside the target class, and labels may contain arbitrary noise.
Sterkenburg supplies a decidably representable class of VC dimension one that no such improper learner can learn.
This resolves the question and separates statistical learnability from computability without invoking polynomial-time assumptions.

definitions:
Use \(\mathbb N=\{0,1,\ldots\}\) with its discrete sigma-algebra, and fix an effective enumeration of finite programs for deterministic Turing machines. A total computable binary function is computed by a program that halts on every natural-number input and returns either zero or one. Decidable representability means that there exists a decidable set \(P\) of program codes, every member of which computes such a total binary function, and the set of functions computed by members of \(P\) is exactly \(\mathcal H\). Decidability concerns membership in this selected set of codes, not membership among all programs computing extensionally equal functions.

A sample is a finite ordered sequence \(S=((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_n,y_n))\), encoded as an explicit list of binary natural numbers and binary labels with lengths and separators. Repetitions are allowed. A learner is one deterministic Turing machine which halts on every such sample, including inconsistent samples, and outputs a finite program computing a total function \(A(S):\mathbb N\to\{0,1\}\). Neither training nor prediction has a running-time bound, and the learner has no oracle. Define \(L_D(g)=\Pr_{(x,y)\sim D}[g(x)\ne y]\). The labels can be noisy: no member of the target class need have zero error. All probability in the displayed guarantee is over the independent training examples. The sample threshold \(N\) can depend on the class, learner, accuracy and confidence, but not on \(D\); no computability requirement is imposed on the function choosing these thresholds. This is CPAC learning, rather than the stronger variant requiring computable sample complexity.

A finite set \(E\subset\mathbb N\) is shattered if every binary labeling of \(E\) is the restriction of a member of \(\mathcal H\). The VC dimension is the supremum of \(|E|\) over shattered finite sets, with value infinity if these cardinalities are unbounded.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the existence claim or its negation. An affirmative answer must establish decidable representability and finite VC dimension for its class, and failure of the agnostic guarantee for every allowed learner. A negative answer would establish the guarantee for every class satisfying the hypotheses. Proper-learning impossibility alone is insufficient. The affirmative mathematical answer is already published; the archival record does not claim that its proof has been formalized in Lean.

context_blocks.text: Ordinary PAC theory allows a learning rule to be any mathematical function of its sample. Computable PAC learning requires an actual halting program for training and for each returned predictor. The question is about this basic computability requirement, with no demand for a fast implementation.

Permitting improper predictions matters. Some classes that defeat computable proper learning sit inside larger classes with effective learning rules, so those earlier counterexamples do not settle the improper question. The source explicitly asks for a decidably representable counterexample.

Sterkenburg proves that a class of stage-bounded diagonal-halting indicators is decidably representable, has VC dimension one, and admits no improper agnostic CPAC learner. Each indicator uses only a finite bounded computation; the failure lies in learning the entire class uniformly across data distributions.

The same paper distinguishes existence of a sample-complexity threshold from an effective procedure computing one. The counterexample excludes the weaker CPAC notion already, so it is not merely a consequence of requiring a computable convergence rate.
